title: AIR sends first autonomous cargo eVTOL to U.S. headquarters for flight demonstrations
summary: This shipment represents a significant step in advancing AIR’s expansion across commercial and defense aviation in the United States.
body_markdown:
[AIR VEV](https://www.airev.aero/) , an aerospace and defense OEM developing and manufacturing electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, today announced the shipment of its first AIR 120D autonomous cargo aircraft to the United States for flight demonstrations at its Florida headquarters.


This shipment represents a significant step in advancing AIR’s expansion across commercial and defense aviation in the United States. The cargo platform is backed by customer deliveries and hundreds of development flights.


The delivery builds on AIR’s partnership with the Florida Department of Transportation and the state’s investment in infrastructure for advanced air mobility. Bringing the AIR 120D to Florida advances plans to establish aircraft production and flight operations at AIR’s headquarters.


This connects the state’s aviation resources with continued development and demonstration of autonomous aerial cargo technology.


Designed to transport cargo without an onboard pilot, the AIR 120D can carry approximately 550 pounds of payload in a 70-cubic-foot cargo bay. Its vertical takeoff and landing capabilities allow it to operate without a runway, supporting missions such as remote resupply, maritime logistics, commercial mid-mile delivery, and humanitarian aid.


The aircraft falls within the U.S. Department of War Group 4 UAS category and is designed to address logistics needs in contested and infrastructure-limited environments.


“Florida has committed to building the infrastructure advanced aviation needs, and bringing the AIR 120D here is a concrete step toward putting that infrastructure to work,” said Rani Plaut, CEO and co-founder of AIR.


“Our cargo program has grown through hundreds of flights and direct customer feedback. Bringing that experience to our U.S. headquarters gives us a foundation to demonstrate how autonomous aircraft can move substantial payloads into difficult-to-reach locations and support a broader range of logistics and defense missions.”


AIR’s cargo platform builds on more than two years of operational development, with flight experience and customer feedback informing its propulsion, battery systems, avionics, and autonomous flight capabilities.


The company announced the first flight of its production cargo configuration in April 2026, following development and operations with earlier aircraft.


The program reflects an important area of innovation in electric aviation, combining autonomous flight with the payload capacity and vertical flight capabilities needed for practical cargo missions. Demonstrating these capabilities in the United States will support AIR’s work to develop repeatable cargo operations and advance an aircraft platform engineered for scalable production.


AIR announced its Florida headquarters partnership in August, outlining plans to bring flight programs for both the AIR ONE personal eVTOL and its autonomous cargo aircraft to the facility. The AIR 120D shipment advances that expansion, strengthening Florida’s role as a base for developing, demonstrating, and ultimately manufacturing AIR’s aircraft in the United States.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by AIR VEV.*
